446	3 Evaluation
447	Our current corpus contains snapshots generated by
448	fuzzing Unicorn and XED with libFuzzer and a num-
449	ber of random snapshots produced by ifuzz—about
450	500,000 in total. The corpus has been deployed to a
451	large portion of the Google production ﬂeet and de-
452	tected multiple faulty machines. We only consider
453	a machine defective if we are able to reproduce the
454	same problem on the same core(s) over multiple
455	days. In about 70% of the cases a single pair of
456	logical cores sharing the same physical core is
457	affected. In most other cases only a single logical
458	core is affected. In just a handful of cases we ob-
459	serve many different cores failing. Some snapshots
460	have detected defects on more than one machine, al-
461	though those defects are not necessarily equivalent.
462	We were able to group some of the defects detected
463	by different snapshots based on similar behavior
464	and likely similar causes.
465	Some machines ﬂagged by SiliFuzz have been
466	independently conﬁrmed as defective by other tests.
467	Others have been implicated in production incidents.
468	Finally, about 45% of SiliFuzz ﬁndings are unique
469	and have not been previously identiﬁed by any other
470	tool or automation available to us. The data we
471	collected ﬂeetwide shows a wide distribution of
472	time-to-failure (CPU time consumed by SiliFuzz
473	on a given machine before detecting the ﬁrst defect)
474	with some machines failing almost immediately and
475	others taking days to detect a single defect.
476	We have observed that our approach of fuzzing
477	by proxy ﬁnds more defects compared to purely
478	random snapshots produced by ifuzz. Preliminary
479	data collected from the quarantine pool shows that
480	from the machines identiﬁed by SiliFuzz, about 40%
481	were uniquely identiﬁable by snapshots produced
482	from Unicorn and XED. About 20% were similarly
483	identiﬁed only by ifuzz-produced snapshots. The
484	remaining 40% of the machines were detectable
485	by both types of snapshots. This suggests that the
486	two types of snapshots are largely complementary.
487	Our insight is that CPU defects are common enough
488	that any sufﬁciently non-trivial fuzzing will uncover
489	some defects when applied at large scale. The twice
490	as many defects found by fuzzing trivial proxies
491	compared to using a sophisticated generation-based
492	fuzzer suggests that fuzzing by proxy is worth fur-
493	ther investigation, especially searching for better
494	proxies.
495	Analyzing CPU defects is a labor-intensive task
496	that is often hindered by poor reproducibility and
497	complicated processes around getting access to spe-
498	ciﬁc production machines. In Appendices A-D we
499	describe four groups of defects that we analyzed
500	in detail. The ﬁrst three affect more than one ma-
501	chine each. The fourth defect falls into a pattern that
502	we observe on multiple machines, but the precise
503	behavior is unique. Defect A was uncovered by a
504	Unicorn-produced snapshot, Defect B was uncov-
505	ered by a XED-produced snapshot, and Defects C
506	& D were independently uncovered by ifuzz- and
507	Unicorn-produced snapshots. We cannot guarantee
508	this attribution with certainty, because early in the
509	project we did cross-pollination between the three
510	corpora. Going forward, we will need to more care-
511	fully track attribution of defects in the presence of
512	cross-pollination.
513	We have detected many other defects that we
514	did not analyze in detail, however we noticed some
515	common patterns:
516	• Wrong results for integer, ﬂoating point and vec-
517	tor instructions. Often the result has just one in-
518	correct bit.
519	• Spurious SIGFPE, SIGSEGV, or SIGILL.
520	• Missing ﬂoating point exception.
521	• No SIGILL where one should be raised according
522	to the speciﬁcation.
523	• Sticky ﬂags, i.e. certain bits in EFLAGS or similar
524	status registers are always set despite the lack of
525	the underlying condition.
526	• Undershooting REP(NE)-preﬁxed string instruc-
527	tions.
528	• Floating point data pointer register (RDP) value
529	mismatch.

544	4 Related Work
545	The SDC problem with electrical defects in micro-
546	processors was known from at least the 1960s. It
547	became more widely known at least two decades
548	ago [23, 5]. Today, for large service providers own-
549	ing multiple data centers, SDC-inducing defects
550	are a very real problem. Facebook discusses their
551	SDC issue in [6] while Google provides a high level
552	overview of SDC in [7].
553	Miller, Fredriksen, and So [24] ﬁrst introduced
554	fuzz testing. Since then, there has been much
555	progress in this area. Readers can refer to [25] for
556	a recent survey of fuzzing techniques. Our work
557	draws on some previous work. In essence, SiliFuzz
558	is a form of differential testing [10], which uses
559	identical test inputs to discover differences between
560	test subjects. It also heavily relies on advances in
561	coverage-guided mutation-based (or “evolutionary”)
562	fuzzing [26].
563	There has been some previous work in fuzzing
564	CPU hardware. Sandsifter [27] uses depth-ﬁrst-
565	search-based fuzzing and page fault analysis to
566	exhaustively determine x86 instruction lengths on
567	CPUs from various vendors. This is done to de-
568	tect undocumented instructions and hardware bugs.
569	Sandsifter focuses on instruction encoding as op-
570	posed to validating the functionality. Easdon [28]
571	describes a way of detecting undocumented instruc-
572	tions only accessible to an operating system’s ker-
573	nel. UISFuzz [29] is another hardware instruction
574	set fuzzer for undocumented instructions similar to
575	Sandsifter. It uses instruction format information
576	to speed up search. Like Sandsifter, it focuses on
577	instruction encoding.
578	Generation-based fuzzing has been applied to
579	hardware for several decades [14, 13]. However, in
580	the past, it typically did not utilize coverage feed-
581	back to guide mutations. More recently, Trippel et
582	al. [1] have translated an RTL design into a software
583	model and applied off-the-shelf coverage-guided
584	software fuzzing engines to the model. Our work
585	uses a real CPU as the fuzz target, for which we
586	do not have the original RTL design. A similar
587	approach to ours was adopted by Martignoni et al.
588	[30] but in the opposite direction. They used a real
589	CPU as the golden reference to perform differential
590	testing to ﬁnd bugs in CPU emulators.
591	While pre- and post-silicon manufacturing tests
592	are performed by CPU vendors before CPUs are
593	delivered to customers [31, 32, 13, 14, 33], SiliFuzz
594	aims to ﬁnd defects in CPUs already deployed in
595	production systems. Crucially, unlike system-level
596	testing performed by CPU vendors, SiliFuzz has
597	to work without the vendors’ expertise, tools, and
598	knowledge and instead leverage a large ﬂeet of de-
599	ployed CPUs at scale—which often is infeasible in
600	pre-production veriﬁcation.
601	5 Future Work
602	We are just starting our work on ﬁnding CPU defects.
603	Future work will be concentrated along four axes:
604	scale, speed, automation, and quality, with quality
605	being the most challenging.
606	Scale
607	We need to run on as many cores for as much time
608	as possible. This is expensive, and we are looking
609	for ways to reduce the cost.
610	Speed
611	The player needs to be further optimized to execute
612	more snapshots per second, and reduce syscalls and
613	I/O operations. Slow-executing snapshots need to
614	be removed without sacriﬁcing the combined proxy
615	code coverage.
616	7
617	
618	===== PAGE 8 =====
619	
620	Automation
621	Detected defects need to be automatically analyzed,
622	deduplicated and reported. Defective machines need
623	to be automatically evicted from the ﬂeet without
624	false positives. CPU vendors need to be provided
625	with actionable reports, reproducers, and often the
626	hardware itself.
627	Quality
628	Quality of the corpus is a function of two values:
629	coverage it provides, and time needed to execute
630	it (or, simply, its size). If the corpus is too large,
631	it becomes too expensive to execute all of it on all
632	cores. If the coverage is low, we will not ﬁnd many
633	defects. There are many ways we can increase the
634	coverage while maintaining a tolerable size.
635	Mutation strategies. We currently mutate the in-
636	struction sequences as simple byte sequences. This
637	is interesting from the point of view of stressing
638	the CPU instruction decoders (or maximizing the
639	coverage of XED), but produces too many invalid
640	instruction sequences. They are mostly not added to
641	the corpus since they generate little new coverage,
642	but they slow down the corpus generation due to
643	the high volume of such snapshots under the current
644	fuzzing strategies. We will need to add structure-
645	aware mutations that produce only valid x86_64
646	sequences. Specialized snapshot mutation strategies
647	are also expected to have a strong effect (see e.g.
648	“register scrambling” from [34]). Cross-pollinating
649	snapshots generated by different proxies is likely
650	to have a positive effect, and we already do it in a
651	limited way via dictionaries.
652	Corpus distillation, a process of choosing the
653	smallest corpus subset while maintaining coverage.
654	Individual corpora coming from Unicorn and XED
655	are already distilled, but their combination may have
656	redundancies. We currently do not distill the ifuzz
657	corpus at all. As we start using more sources of
658	snapshots (e.g. harvesting snapshots from real pro-
659	grams) we will need an efﬁcient distillation strategy,
660	via better coverage metrics and better proxies.
661	Better coverage metrics. Code coverage, while
662	the best we have for software testing, is not a very
663	strong metric of corpus quality. Even when a piece
664	of software has 100% control ﬂow edge coverage,
665	it may still have bugs not detectable by the test cor-
666	pus. Complete code coverage of the software proxy
667	in our approach guarantees even less when testing
668	the hardware. We may be able to develop or reuse
669	better metrics speciﬁcally for fuzzing CPUs. We
670	will continue to rely on software proxies, but ide-
671	ally we would also collect coverage metrics directly
672	from hardware. However, we are likely to remain
673	constrained by the CPUs being mostly opaque to us.
674	Better proxies. XED only allows fuzzing the
675	decoder-like functionality of CPUs. Unicorn is a
676	functional CPU simulator and thus does not give
677	any coverage feedback for the microarchitectural
678	behavior. We will need to ﬁnd ways to fuzz mi-
679	croarchitectural models, e.g. based on gem5 [35] or
680	Simics [36].
681	Quality of the player . The player currently exe-
682	cutes multiple snapshots in the same process (har-
683	ness) with non-trivial set up code in between. We
684	expect that minimizing this set up code will im-
685	prove our chances to ﬁnd defects since every snap-
686	shot execution will then inherit random microarchi-
687	tectural state from previously executed snapshots.
688	We can improve further by running multiple non-
689	overlapping snapshots in parallel threads, such that
690	we stress cache coherency and similar subsystems.
691	Multi-state. Currently we discard a considerable
692	number of snapshots (up to 20%) because they con-
693	tain multiple end states. These can be caused by
694	nondeterminism in these snapshots or by meaning-
695	ful microarchitectural differences. Being able to
696	differentiate the two (e.g. by statically analyzing the
697	disassembled code of each snapshot) will further
698	improve the quality of our snapshot corpus.
699	Bugs vs. defects. SiliFuzz may potentially be used
700	for ﬁnding CPU bugs. Unlike electrical defects,
701	logic bugs can be detected on a single CPU, or even
702	on a CPU model, before the actual CPU even exists.
703	For example, our system can easily reproduce the
704	JCC bug [2] and thus, theoretically, can ﬁnd it too.
705	However, in order to reliably detect bugs we need
706	to allow snapshots with multiple end states and dis-
707	tinguish valid differences between end states (e.g.
708	one CPU family not supporting a given instruction)
709	from differences caused by a bug.

714	6 Conclusion
715	In this paper we presented our work-in-progress sys-
716	tem for ﬁnding CPU defects. We fuzz proxies, such
717	as software CPU simulators and disassemblers, us-
718	ing traditional software fuzzing techniques, and then
719	use the accumulated corpus to cross-check millions
720	of CPU cores. We have detected a large number of
721	defects, analyzed four of them in detail, and ana-
722	lyzed common patterns among the others.
723	We expect this and similar technologies to be
724	in widespread use in the coming years since CPU
725	defects are here to stay.

886	The ﬁrst defect we found with SiliFuzz is related to
887	the F2XM1 x87 instruction, which computes 2x − 1

898	F2XM1 instruction matters. It does not matter if the
899	input comes from an FLDLN2 instruction or loaded
900	from memory. On a given machine, we observed
901	that failures only appear occasionally on the defec-

903	for a given physical core but vary between affected
904	cores. The precise underlying failing mechanism
905	is still unknown to us. We have also conﬁrmed
906	the fault with a vendor-supplied diagnostic tool,

908	we found.

913	tion

916	ports numerous instruction preﬁxes that can be ap-
917	plied only to some instructions, and not to others.
918	In normal circumstances, a preﬁx followed by an
919	incompatible instruction would always raise an ille-
920	gal instruction fault (#UD). We observed some ma-
921	chines sometimes overshoot past these ill-formed
922	instructions without raising a #UD fault.
923	These snapshots originated from fuzzing the x86
924	disassembler, which explains why they contain ille-
925	gal instructions. While this is technically a defect, as
926	the CPUs involved did not behave according to spec-
927	iﬁcations, the problem does not affect normal oper-
928	ation of our ﬂeet because typical production code
929	does not contain illegal instructions. It is still possi-
930	ble that the same defect has another, more harmful,
931	manifestation that we did not observe.

201	SDCs have become a common concern, impacting critical
202	infrastructures [1], [5], [33]. They are now increasingly linked
203	to CPU chips alongside memory, storage, and networking.
204	These corruptions are termed ’silent’ because they escape
205	hardware-level detection mechanisms, causing errors that may
206	propagate through the system unnoticed until they manifest
207	as application-level issues, leading to potential data loss [1],
208	[2]. SDCs may arise from various factors like soft errors,
209	manufacturing defects, and design ﬂaws. They often go un-
210	noticed since the software does not always check for them,
211	especially in cloud and data center environments. Redundancy
212	methods, such as duplicating or triplicating execution, can help
213	mitigate SDCs, but they come with performance and power
214	costs. Both software and hardware-based redundancy methods

222	B. Defects, Faults, Errors
223	A fault models a physical mechanism that leads to a
224	mismatch between a speciﬁcation and the delivered service; in
225	a CPU the service is the correct execution of programs. Every
226	fault has a physical root cause, and in the case of processor
227	faults, high-energy particles like neutrons or alpha particles,
228	as well as silicon manufacturing defects or device lifetime
229	degradation, are well-understood root causes. The temporal
230	behavior of a fault - transient, intermittent, or permanent - is
231	closely tied to its physical root cause (”a bit” in the deﬁnitions
232	refers either to a storage element or to a gate output) [18], [34],
233	[35]. The following fault types (in terms of their temporal
234	behavior) are widely used; we use the broad term fault type
235	instead of fault model to imply only the temporal behavior
236	(duration of existence) of faults and not their logical behavior.
237	1) Transient faults exist for a ﬁnite period of time (disap-
238	pear when the bit is overwritten) and are nonrecurring.
239	2) Intermittent faults oscillate between faulty and fault-free
240	operation.
241	3) Permanent faults do not correct over time (constantly
242	stuck-at faults) [36].
243	In the context of hardware faults, errors are observable
244	outcomes stemming from faults in hardware resources like
245	storage elements or gates. When a defective resource is used
246	during computation, it can lead to Silent Data Corruption
247	(SDC), system crashes, error notiﬁcations, or corrections
248	through hardware resilience mechanisms like Error Correcting
249	Codes (ECC). SDC is the most dangerous outcome, as it can
250	potentially compromise the correctness of software running
251	on the hardware without any observable indication of the
252	error [10]. In the realm of Reliability, Availability, and Ser-
253	viceability (RAS) design for CPUs, emphasis has been placed
254	on mitigating particle-induced faults, often referred to as
255	“soft errors” [37]. However, recent reports from hyperscalers
256	highlight new fault causes, such as marginal defects, capable
257	of inducing faults under speciﬁc conditions like temperature,
258	voltage, and workload patterns [10], [11], [38], [39]. These
259	defects, along with device degradation in scaled technologies,
260	pose severe concerns for transient, intermittent, and permanent
261	faults over a processor’s lifespan. To ensure high reliability,
262	it is crucial to comprehend various physical root causes, their
263	associated fault types, and the resulting errors based on the
264	location of these faults within a processor.
265	C. Fault Detection Capability and Hardware Coverage
266	Fault detection capability of a program in a hardware
267	structure for a speciﬁc fault type or model, is the fraction
268	of the faults in the structure that the program detects (i.e., the
269	faulty run of a diagnostic program deviates from the fault-
270	free run). Detection capability is measured in our simulation
271	infrastructure through statistical fault injection. If N faults are
272	injected and the program detects n of them, its detection capa-
273	bility is n/N. For our fault injection runs in the experimental
274	evaluation, we use the latest version of the gem5-based injector
275	(GeFIN) [40] employed in many reliability studies [41]–[47];
276	a major extension of the tool is the injection of faults in gate
277	level models of CPU functional units.
278	Hardware coverage (for the purposes of our methodology)
279	is deﬁned as any objective (reward) function tied to a speciﬁc
280	CPU hardware structure of any granularity (bit, register, cache
281	line, functional unit, decoder, etc.) that is expected to correlate
282	well with the fault detection capability of functional programs
283	targeting the structure. Coverage functions can incorporate
284	different measures of utilization (both spatial and temporal)
285	in the relevant hardware unit but need to be measured quickly
286	to facilitate iterative reﬁnement of program generation 3.
287	Thus, coverage is a generic ﬁrst-order (fast to measure)
288	hardware proxy employed by our method to grade and enhance
289	the fault detection capability of programs, which is the metric
290	employed in the eventual evaluation of the quality of the
291	programs that Harpocrates generates. Coverage is essentially
292	a proxy of the ability of a program to both activate (sensitize)
293	faults and make them observable (propagate).
294	D. Fault Types Interplay and Coverage Measurement
295	Fig. 2 shows the relationship among fault types used to
296	model silicon defect mechanisms. Ideally, a perfect functional
297	test program would detect all fault types across all hardware
298	areas, including faults that arise during the CPU’s lifetime
299	but were not present during manufacturing. The diagram’s
300	“transients” area encompasses all fault combinations over time
301	(i.e., all combinations of a [bit] x [cycles of fault existence]),
302	representing the entire fault universe. Permanent faults are a
303	subset of transients (i.e., the cycles the fault exists is equal to
304	the total program cycles), persisting throughout the program.
305	Intermittent faults exist for a speciﬁc number of cycles and
306	can behave as permanent or transient within that interval. A
307	program that detects all transient faults is also very likely 4 to
308	detect the other two types of faults in a hardware bit.
309	To this end, to guide the Harpocrates methodology for
310	array-based components, we focus on a hardware coverage
311	metric related to transient faults. Architecturally Correct Exe-
312	cution (ACE) analysis [16], [48], [49] identiﬁes the fraction of
313	bits crucial for correct execution thus estimating the program’s
314	vulnerability to transient faults [50]. The ACE lifetime analysis
315	computes, in each cycle (incorporating the notion of time
316	which is needed for transient faults), the bits that are necessary
317	for Architecturally Correct Execution (ACE) and labels them
318	as ACE. We use the ACE lifetime analysis result (the “vulner-
319	ability”; ranging from 0 to 1 or 0% to 100%) as our hardware

359	E. Measuring Fault Detection Capability
360	We employ Statistical Fault Injection (SFI) to estimate a
361	program’s fault detection capability. SFI injects faults at the
362	microarchitecture level and observes outcomes at the software
363	level [45], [51]–[54]. This approach assesses a program’s
364	ability to detect hardware faults across the layers. In particular,
365	if the injected fault propagates to the output of the program
366	without any observable indication, the effect is a Silent Data
367	Corruption (SDC). Another case is when the injected fault
368	propagates to the software and results in an Application or
369	System Crash. Conversely, if the fault is masked at either
370	the hardware or software level, it remains undetected. CPU
371	protection schemes like parity and ECC are considered in
372	fault injection modeling. For example, a single bit ﬂip in a
373	fully unprotected cache will be either Masked or lead to an
374	SDC or Crash, while in a SECDED (single error correction
375	double error detection) cache it will be Masked (Corrected).
376	For different fault types (e.g., transient or permanent faults),
377	we grade the ﬁnal fault detection capability of the reﬁned
378	functional programs of Harpocrates using this approach.
379	III. E XISTING FRAMEWORKS AND EXPERIMENTAL SETUP
380	A. Open-Source CPU Testing Frameworks
381	Aiming to drive community-wide efforts in improving
382	defects detection in CPUs, some open-source frameworks,
383	contributed by the industry, have been publicly released. Many
384	of these test frameworks have been released to the community
385	through the broad industry-wide effort in the context of the
386	Open Compute Project (OCP) and are summarized in [55].

404	like) software proxies like CPU simulators and disassemblers.
405	It uses software-coverage metrics to create a diverse input
406	set, known as the corpus. High code coverage in proxies, is
407	conjectured to uncover interesting CPU behavior and detect
408	defects. Silifuzz is hardware and ISA agnostic, generating

410	deterministic result programs are retained as snapshots to run
411	on the CPU. While still a work in progress, SiliFuzz is yielding
412	results in the ﬁeld. To achieve statistically signiﬁcant results in
413	our fault injection-based evaluation, instructions from multiple
414	snapshots (maximum of 100 bytes of binary code each) are
415	aggregated into a single 10K instructions test (the typical size

417	2) OpenDCDiag [56]: OpenDCDiag is an open-source
418	project designed for identifying defects and bugs in CPUs,

420	consists of a set of manually speciﬁed tests built around a
421	CPU testing framework. The framework permits the addition
422	of custom, user-speciﬁed tests, offering convenient primi-
423	tives. The open-source tests provided include compression,
424	cryptographic operations, matrix multiplication and singular
425	value decomposition. These algorithms are sensitive to data
426	corruption; corruption in their inputs or intermediate results is
427	highly likely to result in corruption in the output data.
428	In our evaluation of OpenDCDiag we consider each test
429	separately, and evaluate a single execution of the full test.
430	Input sizes are conﬁgured so that no test exceeds 100 million
431	cycles of execution.

437	methodologies to reﬁne and measure the hardware coverage
438	and the detection capability of Harpocrates-generated pro-
439	grams. Both the coverage and the detection capability can
440	highlight the ability to detect faults and identify the cause of a

442	the widely used gem5 simulator [57]–[59], which is a well-
443	established microarchitectural simulator. We extend the gem5
444	simulator to allow the evaluation of the ACE lifetime analysis
445	and the IBR metric (presented in II-D), as well as the injection
446	of faults of different types in the microarchitectural structures.

904	Moreover, in x86, we have to consider the implicit operands
905	of instructions when encoding them. For example, in x86-
906	64, some variants of the MUL instruction implicitly store
907	part of their result in RAX. If this case is disregarded, the
908	code generator will be unable to prevent a situation like the
909	following: Assume the RAX register is used as an address base
910	register, but the generator inserts a MUL instruction. In this
911	case, a segmentation fault is very likely during execution, as
912	the address is most likely corrupted after the MUL operation.
913	Stack-related instructions like PUSH and POP and their
914	variants can also produce crashing sequences, e.g., popping the
915	empty stack. A related issue was the resulting stack alignment
916	after the execution of the generated sequence. For x86-64
917	(or amd64) architecture, the stack alignment ABI requires the
918	stack to be aligned on a 16-byte boundary when a function is
919	called. We carefully insert a re-aligning snippet of instructions
920	after the end of our generated sequence.
921	To detect corruptions, it is important to provide programs
922	with deterministic output (i.e., executions of the program
923	always provide the same output). To achieve this, the code
924	generator excludes certain x86-64 instructions that are non-
925	deterministic (as the authors of SiliFuzz also pointed out).

936	replaces all the occurrences of a randomly selected instruction
937	of the sequence, with another random instruction (the same
938	mnemonics with different operand types are handled as distinct
939	instructions). This strategy provides fairness in replacement
940	due to the uniform selection of the replacement instruction.
941	This policy’s beneﬁts are twofold: (1) We can optimize any
942	objective function without tuning the mutation strategy sep-
943	arately, (2) We avoid the pitfall of specifying “too explicit”
944	mutation strategies that would trivialize programs and narrow
945	the explored ISA space or get stuck in local optima. The
946	counterargument might be that a “targeted” mutation strategy
947	converges faster, however, as we present in the evaluation sec-
948	tion VI, our instruction replacement policy converges swiftly,
949	without the aforementioned pitfalls.

954	constrained random generation, whereas the more interesting
955	ﬂows involve the mutation engine as well. For example,

958	instruction sequence of each generated program 5 times, 3)
959	Generate programs from the 25 total mutated sequences, etc.;

972	evaluation/grading platform (III-B). Utilizing gem5 enables

975	rich microarchitectural-level data available through simulation

1231	(Silifuzz and OpenDCDiag) and the MiBench workloads are
1232	shown to put things in perspective and showcase how Har-
1233	pocrates can generate tests that adapt to different components
1234	and fault modes, providing excellent detection capability.
1235	1) Integer Register File: the Harpocrates-generated pro-
1236	gram manages to detect nearly 10x more faults compared
1237	to the other frameworks, as shown in the leftmost graph
1238	in Fig. 11. The register ﬁle structure is very challenging
1239	for transient fault detection due to the very high rates of
1240	register allocation and freeing during program execution. Our
1241	uniform random instruction replacement policy guided by
1242	feedback from the ACE coverage metric allows us to generate
1243	instruction patterns that maximize program bits exposed to
1244	transient faults in the IRF. It is evident that these patterns do

1250	Harpocrates’ ﬁnal tests for the data cache manage an even
1251	higher detection capability for transients, approaching 90% .
1252	3) Integer Adder: In this structure, every framework’s best
1253	programs nearly fully detect all gate-level stuck-at faults
1254	injected (with SiliFuzz slightly behind the rest). However, the
1255	average test of the other frameworks provides poor coverage
1256	of the permanent faults (third from the left graph Fig. 11).
1257	4) Integer Multiplier: In this structure, SiliFuzz performs
1258	much better than OpenDCDiag and MiBench, which are
1259	lacking a test with signiﬁcant activity in the integer multiplier.

1261	5) SSE FP Adder: On average across MiBench, SiliFuzz
1262	and OpenDCDiag the detection capability of SSE FP adder
1263	faults is low, as seen in the second from the right graph of
1264	Fig. 11, mainly due to lack of SSE activity in most workloads
1265	as mentioned in Sec. III-C. There are multiple outlier programs
1266	(mainly in OpenDCDiag) that achieve high detection capabil-
1267	ity in this component (up to 98.5%). Harpocrates achieves
1268	99.8% detection in orders-of-magnitude less CPU cycles.
1269	6) SSE FP Multiplier: Similarly to the adder, SSE FP
1270	multiplier detection capability is even lower on average for
1271	non-Harpocrates workloads. In contrast to the adder, maximum
1272	detection capability is achieved by a single OpenDCDiag
1273	program and is only 58.2%, very low for permanent faults.
1274	The Harpocrates generated program reaches 99.7% detection.
1275	Overall, Harpocrates is the only framework to manage nearly
1276	full fault detection in all functional units we compared .

1279	metrics outlined in Section II-D. For bit array components,
1280	ACE serves as a coverage metric that establishes an upper

1282	between the coverage and detection capability of our generated

Read these files (each is a full extracted paper text) and summarize them:
- /tmp/reftext/harpocrates1.txt  (Harpocrates: Automated Functional Program Generation Against CPU Faults and SDCs — this is likely a newer/shorter companion)
- /tmp/reftext/sosp23.txt  (Understanding SDCs in a Large Production CPU Population — Google/Meta fleet study)
- /tmp/reftext/veritas.txt  (Veritas: Demystifying SDCs — arch-level modeling + fleet data of modern x86)

content.text:
我现在已经掌握了全面的情报。让我整合一下关键发现，并找出当前 paper2 与“最佳论文”标准之间的差距。

**关键竞争情报总结：**

1. **SiliFuzz** (基准)：基于 Unicorn 代理 + XED/ifuzz，覆盖率引导但**操作数无方向性**的变异 (`FlipRandomBit` 在完整的指令字上随机位翻转；TODO 确认仅存在一种内容变异模式)。x86_64。已在源码中验证：`fuzzer/program_mutation_ops.cc:187` 的 TODO，以及将 Kunpeng `0x48` 强制映射为 N1。

2. **Harpocrates-HIL (ISCA'24)** — *最近且最危险的竞争对手*。使用 gem5-SFI + ACE/IBR 适应度，MuSeqGen (基于 MicroProbe 的 x86 生成器)，指令替换变异。**其评估方法与当前的 paper2 相同** (gem5 + SFI + ACE)。结果：30倍于 SiliFuzz 的生成率；在整数加法器上达到 99% 的检测率，仅需 5 万个周期，而 MiBench 需要 1100 万个周期；在检测率上比最佳 SiliFuzz 测试 (86.6%) 高出 99.5%。**差距：仅限 x86，仅限 gem5，没有真实的缺陷芯片**。

3. **关键发现**：已发布的 CHAOS 论文**并不包含 CHAOSLSQFwd / byte_lane_skew** —— 这是来自 Paper 1 的扩展。当前的 paper2 将其作为结构性指标，必须将其记录为我们自己的贡献（或追溯到 Paper 1），而不能仅引用 CHAOS。

4. 竞争对手中存在的主要空白：ITHICA（不一致的错误，Google 舰队，x86），SEVI（向量 SDC，Meta，x86），PinDrop（持续特征描述，Meta），Orthrus（在线重新执行，SOSP'25）——全部**仅限 x86**。**ARM 服务级 SDC 检测生成**是一个真正的开放领域。

现在让我看看现有的 paper2 实际工件（workloads、scripts、results），以确切了解我们拥有哪些数据，然后检查 kunpeng920 研究报告。让我同时阅读第一篇 Harpocrates 论文和 kunpeng 报告。

17	engine that models and grades for multiple fault types. Harpocrates adapts to

296	Tools
297	Stepping through the components in the order they 
298	were presented in the overview of the previous section, 
299	the Generator and Mutator are mapped to our code 
300	generator and mutator MuSeqGen. For the purposes 
301	of this study, we have configured MuSeqGen for x86-64 
302	assembly program generation and mutation. Mutation 
303	was experimentally found to be optimal with respect to 
304	convergence when performed via random instruction 
305	replacement. More specifically, all instances of instruc-
306	tion A are replaced by a randomly sampled instruction 
307	B. At a high level, the generator constructs programs 
308	by emitting sequences of instructions that satisfy ba -
309	sic correctness constraints (valid opcodes, valid regis-
310	ter, immediate and memory operands). The operands 
311	are selected based on a static policy. For example, im-
312	mediate operands are always sampled randomly from 
313	their whole range (e.g., any 16-bit number for a 16-bit 
314	immediate). The mutation operator then explores the 
315	neighborhood of a candidate program by replacing all 
316	instances of one instruction kind with another ran-
317	domly sampled kind, a coarse-grained mutation that 
318	empirically balances exploration with maintaining pro-
319	gram validity. We refer the interested reader to the orig-
320	inal Harpocrates article8 for an in-depth description of 
321	the architecture and inner workings of MuSeqGen.
322	The final and arguably most critical component in 
323	the pipeline is the Evaluator. In our concrete pipeline, 
324	our custom version of gem5 assumes the role of the 
325	Evaluator. We have enriched the base microarchitec-
326	tural modeling engine of gem5 with various analyses 
327	and metrics, allowing us to construct hardware-aware 
328	fitness functions that are highly targeted to specific 
329	hardware structures. Optimizing for suitable fitness 
330	functions allows Harpocrates to converge to programs 
331	with high detection capability in the target component.
332	Coverage, Detection, and Fault Models
333	For the purposes of this study, we shall refer to the 
334	hardware-aware fitness functions we construct as 
335	hardware coverage or simply coverage. We define this 
336	as follows: Hardware coverage is any objective (fit -
337	ness) function tied to a specific CPU hardware struc-
338	ture that is expected to correlate well with the fault 
339	detection capability of functional programs targeting 
340	the structure. Coverage is essentially a proxy of the 
341	ability of a program to both activate (sensitize) faults 
342	and make them observable (propagate).
343	gem5’s purpose in this study is twofold: First, our en-
344	riched gem5 is used to measure the hardware coverage 
345	(fitness function) we have tailored to the target compo-
346	nent and fault type. Second, we utilize our fault injection 
347	infrastructure built around gem5 to accurately measure 
348	the detection capability of programs for a specific fault 
349	type and hardware structure. Our infrastructure can inject 
350	transient (single bit-flips, overwritable; usually particle 
351	strike induced), permanent (stuck-at faults, non-overwrit-
352	able), or intermittent (exist for a specific number of cycles 
353	and can behave as permanent or transient) faults in more 
354	than 50 microarchitectural targets. Further, we can inject 
355	gate-level stuck-at faults in the functional units of the CPU. 
356	The fault detection capability of programs is assessed via 
357	statistical fault injection (SFI). By conducting thousands 
358	of injection experiments in the selected hardware struc-
359	ture, we obtain a statistically significant, reliable, “golden” 
360	measure of a program’s ability to detect faults.
361	An important observation here is to highlight the 
362	impracticality of a flow that would refine programs by 
363	directly measuring detection capability through SFI. 
364	Such a flow would require several hours for just a single 
365	iteration, in contrast to the fast iteration speed (often 
366	in the range of seconds or even subseconds) offered 
367	by Harpocrates. This is precisely the reason we have 
368	constructed proxy metrics—which are measurable in 
369	a single program execution—to optimize instead.
370	To evaluate Harpocrates we have chosen seven 
371	key hardware structures comprising both bit-array

现在我已经掌握了竞争格局的全貌。两篇 Harpocrates 论文实质上都是相同的 ISCA'24 工作（“Harpocrates++”是对其的 IEEE Micro 扩展）。它们都使用 x86 + gem5 + SFI + ACE/IBR。

**目前关键的战略洞察**是：现有的 paper2 在 SiliFuzz 的比较中表述得相当好，但它有一个致命的弱点，阻碍了其成为“最佳论文”——**它与 Harpocrates-HIL 的竞争不够充分**，而后者：
1. 使用了相同的评估方法（gem5+SFI+ACE）
2. 拥有更丰富的故障模型（通过 SFI 对 50 多种微架构结构和门级 FU 进行建模，而当前的 paper2 仅有 2 种注入器）
3. 实现了 99%+ 的检测率（相比之下，当前 paper2 在 bit-flip 上最好的结果是 24.6%）
4. 拥有更正式的生成器（MuSeqGen/MicroProbe 对比当前的 paper2 手写 C 语言工作负载）

然而，Harpocrates 存在一些 paper2 可以胜出的弱点：
1. **仅限 x86** — paper2 是 ARM (Kunpeng 920)，这是 ARM 服务器 CPU SDC 的开放前沿
2. **仅限 gem5，没有真实的缺陷硅片** — paper2 在 446 个核心上部署了真实硅片（尽管目前是健康的硅片）
3. **没有真实硅片上的真实 SDC** — Paper 1 的核心 179 法医分析是我们独有的背景事实
4. **没有结构故障模型** — paper2 的 `byte_lane_skew`（来自 Paper 1）是一种真实的缺陷类故障模型，Harpo 没有这一模型；它们的 FU 故障是通用的固定型故障（stuck-at）
5. **没有噪声分类法** — paper2 的 `RunSnapOutcome` 2/3/4 与 5/6 的区别是部署层面的贡献

让我阅读一下 kunpeng920 研究报告（其中可能包含 Paper 1 的核心 179 分析以及关键的实证事实），并核实 D13 数据工件（data artifacts）是否真实存在。

37	## 1. 研究背景与动机
38	
39	### 1.1 SDC 问题概述
40	
41	SDC（Silent Data Corruption）指 CPU 执行指令时产生**错误的计算结果**，但该错误未被任何硬件校验机制（ECC、Parity、Machine Check）捕获，因此静默传播到软件层面。SDC 是数据中心最棘手的硬件缺陷形态——它不崩溃、不告警，却悄悄损坏计算结果。
42	
43	### 1.2 现有检测工具的痛点
44	
45	当前 ARM CPU 的 SDC 检测用例在电路级覆盖率存在明显短板：
46	
47	| 单元 | 覆盖率 | 评级 | 薄弱原因 |
48	|------|--------|------|---------|
49	| FSU（浮点/SIMD） | 80% | 🟢 较好 | 防下限不够，缺乏极致操作数压力 |
50	| IEX（整数单元） | 70% | 🟡 一般 | 缺乏长进位链压测 |
51	| IFU（取指单元） | 66% | 🟡 一般 | 分支预测/BTB 路径覆盖浅 |
52	| OoO（乱序执行） | 56% | 🟠 薄弱 | 均匀指令流填不满 ROB/Issue Queue |
53	| LSU（加载/存储） | 54% | 🟠 薄弱 | 未触发 Store Buffer 前递与跨边界分拆逻辑 |
54	| L2C（L2 Cache） | 40% | 🔴 很弱 | MESI/MOESI 状态机基本未遍历 |
55	| MMU（内存管理） | 20% | 🔴 极弱 | TLB（CAM）/PTW 状态机几乎未覆盖 |
56	
57	**核心痛点**：现有工具仅在"指令集空间"做均匀遍历，未深入"操作数/执行上下文空间"做压力权重覆盖。EDA 工具仿真覆盖率（结构覆盖率：某 Gate 是否被激活过）与真实电路注错覆盖率（功能检出率：Gate 翻转后错误能否传播到输出）是**完全不同的维度**。一条 Gate 即便被激活（结构覆盖率=1），若操作数未触发其最脆弱时序路径，也无法检出瞬态翻转（功能检出率=0）。
58	
59	### 1.3 研究目标
60	
61	突破覆盖率瓶颈，生成"高效精准"的 SDC 检测用例——不仅要点亮 Gate（保覆盖下限），更要激发潜伏的瞬态错误（提检出上限），并在真机上验证检出能力，迭代改进至高检出率。

73	| 因素 | 物理本质 | 检测策略 |
74	|------|----------|----------|
75	| **① 设计期校验冗余不足** | 成本/面积/功耗妥协，部分逻辑路径无 ECC/Parity 保护（ALU 计算路径、TLB CAM 匹配、乱序控制状态机） | 针对无保护路径设计最长组合逻辑延迟的操作数，逼出时序违例 |
76	| **② 老化/工艺退化** | HCI/NBTI/EM 导致晶体管阈值漂移，时序裕量随时间变薄 | 设计高翻转率（Toggle Rate）操作数序列，加速暴露老化失效 |
77	| **③ 业务负载模型** | 特定业务持续激发特定模块（DB→LSU，HPC→FSU，虚拟化→MMU/CSU） | 抽象业务模型，做差异化压力权重分配 |
78	
79	### 2.2 两大范式转移
80	
81	```
82	范式转移 1:  指令集空间 ──→ 操作数/执行上下文空间
83	             (遍历指令类型)    (对每条指令, 遍历操作数的极端值组合)
84	
85	范式转移 2:  均匀覆盖 ──→ 压力权重覆盖
86	             (每模块等权)    (对弱模块施加 3-5 倍权重的测试密度)
87	```
88	
89	**核心洞察**：`add x0, x1, x2` 在结构覆盖率上只算"1 个指令"，但 `x1=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, x2=0x1`（全进位链）与 `x1=0x0, x2=0x0`（零路径）激活的内部 Gate 路径完全不同。操作数空间的深度变异是提升功能检出率的关键杠杆。
90	
91	### 2.3 三维 SDC 压测空间
92	
93	1. **微架构与电路脆弱性维度（Bottom-Up）**：针对缺乏 ECC/Parity 保护的逻辑、高扇出网络、易时序违例的深层流水线定向打击（对应因素 ①②）。
94	2. **执行上下文与指令空间维度（Core）**：通过操作数极端变异、指令乱序重排、复杂数据依赖，最大化电路翻转率，局部制造极端 di/dt，逼出边缘失效。
95	3. **业务负载特征维度（Top-Down）**：抽象数据库（LSU/L2C）、虚拟化（MMU/CSU）、HPC（FSU/IEX）业务模型，按部署场景做权重分配（对应因素 ③）。
96	
97	**破局命题**：只有 Down-Top 与 Top-Down 融合，才能既知"哪里脆弱"又知"现实里它会被怎么打"，把压力精确施加到最该打的地方。

135	|------|---------|----------------------|
136	| V2 | ALU+Complex 端口饱和 | 3 ALU+1 Complex(4-cyc), 33-entry sched |

145	| M3 | 跨 4KB 页边界 LDP | MMU 双 TLB 查询+权限检查 |

151	| O2 | 分支预测欺骗+PRF 回滚 | BPU 训练+误预测+PRF 回滚 |

155	**关键技术修正（实测发现的 AArch64 约束）**：
156	- **分支种子有效**：纠正先前"退出序列要求直链无分支"的假设。实测 `b.eq`/`b.ne`/前向 `b` 均通过 `make`+`runner`，退出序列在 PC 走出代码边界时捕获（非线性递增）。V3/O2/I2 保留分支语义。
157	- **stp/ldp 寻址约束**：只接受 `[Xn,#imm]`（imm 为 8 倍数）或 `[Xn]`，**不接受** `[Xn,Xm]`。跨 16B/64B/128B 边界须先 `add x8,x6,#14` 计算非对齐地址到寄存器，再 `stp x0,x1,[x8]`。`ldr/str` 单寄存器形式可接受 `[Xn,Xm]`。
158	- **立即数上限**：`ldr` 立即数偏移上限 32760，`add` 上限 4095，`movz` 16 位立即数上限 0xFFFF。大偏移用 `movz`+`movk` 装临时寄存器 + `add reg,reg`。
159	- **SnapMaker 页限制**：`max_pages_to_add=5`（默认），硬上限 `kMaxAddedPageAddresses=20`。c1/m1 访问页数压缩到 ≤5 适配默认。

372	## 6. 关键发现与结论
373	
374	### 6.1 方法论验证
375	
376	**设计概念四要素全部工程化落地**：
377	- weak 三因素：19 模板分别对应设计冗余不足（进位链/乘法器最长延迟）、老化（高翻转率 100% bit-toggle）、业务负载（MMU/L2C/LSU 专项）。
378	- 两范式：操作数字典笛卡尔积（指令空间→操作数空间）+ 弱模块专项模板（均匀→压力权重）。
379	- 三维压测空间：Bottom-Up 微架构定向（模板）+ Core 执行上下文（操作数变异）+ Top-Down 业务画像（模块权重）。
380	
381	### 6.2 完整证据链
382	
383	```
384	激发端 (gem5-fi 微架构故障注入)
385	  50 次单 bit 翻转 → 2 diverge (4.0%) → 证明检测用例能被激发出可观测 SDC
386	        ↓
387	检出端 (silifuzz 注错验证)
388	  篡改代码 → runner outcome=3 → 精准报翻转寄存器值 → 证明检出链路对位翻转敏感
389	        ↓
390	真机部署 (分布式满负载扫描)
391	  3 单板 ~446 核 → 总 SDC=0 → 真机健康 (非检出能力不足)
392	```
393	
394	端到端有效：检测用例既能被 gem5-fi 激发，又能被 silifuzz runner 检出，真机部署数据一致。
395	
396	### 6.3 关键技术发现
397	
398	1. **分支种子有效**（纠正先前假设）：snap_tool 退出序列在 PC 走出代码边界时捕获（非线性递增），`b.eq`/`b.ne`/前向 `b` 均可用，V3/O2/I2 保留分支语义。
399	2. **stp/ldp 寻址约束**：仅 `[Xn,#imm(8倍数)]` 或 `[Xn]`，跨边界须先 `add` 计算非对齐地址。
400	3. **静态二进制跨单板部署**：runner+orchestrator `statically linked`，从 0103 拷贝即跑，无需重新编译。
401	4. **满负载 SIGSEGV 容错**：`--max_cpus=$(nproc)` 时资源耗尽击中 snap 外路径，非 SDC，orchestrator 容错继续。
402	5. **满负载日志交织**：多核并发输出致字符交错，须精确正则匹配 `Snapshot [hash] failed, outcome` 避免假阳性。
403	6. **操作数空间变异激活不同 Gate**：e1 carry32 变体 `x0=0x100000000` vs all_ones `x0=0`，证明同指令不同操作数走不同进位链路径。
404

Paper 2's biggest "best-paper" threat is **Harpocrates**, not SiliFuzz. Two papers, same project (Univ. Athens + AMD, Gizopoulos/Gurumurthi):
- `docs/paper/ref/Harpocrates_Breaking_the_Silence...pdf` = ISCA'24 (DOI 10.1109/ISCA59077.2024.00045), 16pp, the full paper.
- `docs/paper/ref/Harpocrates_Automated_Functional_Program_Generation...pdf` = IEEE Micro Jan/Feb 2026 ("Harpocrates++"), 10pp, an extension of the ISCA'24 article.

**Why it's the closest competitor:** same evaluation paradigm as Paper 2 — gem5 + statistical fault injection (SFI) + ACE/IBR fitness. Generator = MuSeqGen (built on MicroProbe, x86-64). Mutation = replace-all-instances-of-instruction-A-with-B. 7 hardware structures (IRF, L1D, LSQ, int add/mul, SSE FP add/mul). >50 µarch SFI targets + gate-level FU stuck-at.

**Harpocrates headline numbers (to NOT claim we beat without measuring):** 30× SiliFuzz generation rate; 99% int-adder detection in 50K cycles vs MiBench's 11M (220× faster); 99.5% vs SiliFuzz-best 86.6% on the multiplier; prefix-slice: permanent FU faults detectable with first 10% of instructions; random-seed variance <1% (most) to ~17% (int mul). Absolute detection ~99% on FUs.

**Harpocrates' gaps = Paper 2's differentiation axes:**
1. **x86-64 only** — Paper 2 is AArch64/Kunpeng920/TaiShan V110 (open ARM-server frontier; all fleet competitors — SOSP23, Veritas, PinDrop, SEVI, Orthrus, ITHICA — are x86).
2. **gem5-only, no real defective silicon** — Paper 2 deploys on 4-board 446-core real Kunpeng920 fleet (even if healthy-silicon 0-SDC); Paper 1's core-179 forensics is real-defect ground truth Harpocrates lacks.
3. **No structural/defect-class fault model** — Harpocrates injects generic bit-flip (transient) + stuck-at (permanent). Paper 2's `byte_lane_skew` (CHAOSLSQFwd) models a *real* defect class (core-179 store-to-load-forwarding). ⚠️ published CHAOS paper (chaos.txt) does NOT contain CHAOSLSQFwd/byte_lane_skew — that's Paper 1's extension; document as our contribution, don't just cite CHAOS.
4. **Static operand policy, no runtime directed-on-random** — Harpocrates resolves operands via static policy + random immediates; Paper 2's D13 `pick_high_toggle` biases operands at runtime toward high-ACE (popcount carry-chain proxy). This is the genuine methodological delta.
5. **No fleet noise taxonomy** — Paper 2's RunSnapOutcome 2/3/4 (genuine SDC) vs 5/6 (runaway/misbehave noise) is a deployment contribution; Harpocrates has no fleet deployment.

**Honest framing for the rewrite:** do NOT claim D13's 24.6% bit-flip / 65.4% structural "beats Harpocrates's 99%". Different fault model, different structure, different ISA — not directly comparable. Claim: "first ARM-server SDC workload generator evaluated under both bit-flip and a real-defect-class structural model, deployed on real silicon." See [[paper2-bestpaper-program]] [[paper2-bbit-honest-recount]].

# Plan: 重构 docs/paper2 为顶会 best-paper（对标 SiliFuzz + 两篇 Harpocrates）

> 本文件是 plan-mode 的产出。执行须遵循 `academic-research-skills:academic-paper` 技能的 8 阶段流水线（Phase 0 配置 → 7 格式化），但适配“重构已有论文 + 真实实验数据已存在”这一现实，而非从零选题。每一阶段的产物落到 `docs/paper2/` 下具体文件。

---

## 0. 现状判定与定位（已在探索期完成）

### 0.1 既有资产盘点（均已核实存在，非虚构）
- `docs/paper/paper2_en.md`（41717 B, 330 行）+ `docs/paper/paper2_zh.md`（37676 B, 329 行）：现有 Paper 2，英文/中文双版本。数据真实，但**对标仅 SiliFuzz，未充分对标 Harpocrates**，且在"best-paper"尺度上有 4 处硬伤（见 §0.3）。
- `docs/kunpeng920_sdc_research_report.md`（36216 B）：研究报告，含 D1–D13 全演进路径 + 真机 4 板 446 核扫描 + gem5-CHAOS 注入全部真实数据。**注意 §7.1 仍写 "D13 bit=24.6% (3.07x)"——这是旧 8.0% 口径的 ratio；on-disk 诚实重计给出 41/500=8.2% / 3.00×（见 memory `paper2-bbit-honest-recount`）。重构须用 3.00× / 8.2%，不得再用 3.07×。**
- `docs/paper/ref/`：17 篇参考文献（全部已 pypdf 抽取到 `/tmp/reftext/`）。三篇对标论文：`silifuzz.pdf`、`Harpocrates_Breaking_the_Silence...pdf`（ISCA'24，16pp）、`Harpocrates_Automated_Functional_Program_Generation...pdf`（IEEE Micro Jan/Feb 2026 "Harpocrates++"，10pp）。
- 真实工件（artifacts）：`seeds/gem5/sdc_probe_workload_d{1..13}.c` + `sdc_probe_workload_random.c`（B 基线）、`scripts/d{1..13}_sweep.py` + `gem5_sweep_*` 注入脚本、`tools/sdc_mutator/evolution_engine.py`（离线演化引擎原型）、`scripts/distributed_scan.py` + `collect_results.py`（4 板部署）、`output/distributed/results.json`。19 个微架构压力模板 `seeds/*.S`（MMU/L2C/LSU/OoO/IEX/FSU/IFU）。
- 源码事实（已由 subagent 逐行核实，见下）：SiliFuzz 变异器 `fuzzer/program_mutation_ops.cc:187` 的 `TODO(ncbray): other mutation modes` 证实**仅实现 bit-flip 一种内容变异**；`util/platform.cc:165-167` 证实 `implementer==0x48`（华为）→ `kArmNeoverseN1` 强制映射；`runner/runner.h:32-43` 证实 `RunSnapOutcome` 7 值（0-6）；`proxies/arch_feature_generator.h:33-42` 证实 `reg_toggle_zero_one/one_zero/reg_difference/op_reg_toggle/op_pair` 全部存在（per-bit toggle 覆盖信号），即 fitness 函数可建于 SiliFuzz 自有代理基板。

### 0.2 竞争情报（已深读三篇对标论文 + 14 篇参考文献）
- **SiliFuzz**：Unicorn 代理 + XED/ifuzz + Centipede；coverage-guided 但**operand-undirected**（`FlipRandomBit` 对整条指令编码做随机位翻转，TODO 证实仅一模式）。x86_64。"we do not claim novelty in the academic sense"；自承"quality"是未来工作开放轴（"register scrambling"、"better metrics specifically for fuzzing CPUs"）。→ 我们正是沿着 SiliFuzz 自己点名的"quality"轴推进。
- **Harpocrates-HIL (ISCA'24) + Harpocrates++ (IEEE Micro'26)**：**最近、最危险的竞品**。MuSeqGen（MicroProbe 之上，x86-64 生成器）+ 指令替换变异 + gem5 评估器 + ACE/IBR fitness + SFI 金标准。7 结构（IRF/L1D/LSQ/int add-mul/SSE FP add-mul）。**评估范式与现 paper2 几乎相同（gem5+SFI+ACE）**。数字：30× SiliFuzz 生成率；99% int-adder 检测仅 50K cycles（vs MiBench 11M，220× faster）；99.5% vs SiliFuzz-best 86.6%；前缀切片实验（permanent FU 故障用前 10% 指令即可检测）；随机种子方差 <1%（多数）至 ~17%（int mul）。
- **关键：Harpocrates 的硬伤 = 我们的差异化轴**：(1) **仅 x86-64** → 我们是 AArch64/鲲鹏920/TaiShan V110（ARM 服务器 SDC 生成是开放前沿；SOSP23/Veritas/PinDrop/SEVI/Orthrus/ITHICA 全是 x86）；(2) **仅 gem5，无真实缺陷硅片** → 我们在 4 板 446 核真机部署 + Paper 1 核心 179 取证是 Harpocrates 缺失的真实缺陷 ground truth；(3) **无结构/缺陷类故障模型** → Harpocrates 注入 generic bit-flip + stuck-at；我们的 `byte_lane_skew`（CHAOSLSQFwd）建模**真实**缺陷类（core-179 store-to-load 前递）。⚠️ **已发表 CHAOS 论文（chaos.txt）不含 CHAOSLSQFwd/byte_lane_skew——这是 Paper 1 的扩展**，须作为本文/本程序的贡献显式说明，不能只引 CHAOS；(4) **静态操作数策略，无 runtime directed-on-random** → Harpocrates 用静态策略 + 随机立即数解析操作数；D13 的 `pick_high_toggle` 在 runtime 把操作数偏向高 ACE（popcount 进位链代理），这是真正的方法论 delta；(5) **无集群噪声分类法** → RunSnapOutcome 2/3/4（真 SDC）vs 5/6（runaway/misbehave 噪声）是部署贡献。
- **诚实框定（防过度声称）**：**不得**声称 D13 的 24.6%/65.4% "击败 Harpocrates 的 99%"——不同故障模型、不同结构、不同 ISA，不可直接比较。正确声称："首个在 ARM 服务器 CPU 上、在 bit-flip 与真实缺陷类结构故障双度量下评估、并在真实硅片集群部署的 SDC 工作负载生成器"。D13 vs B 的 3.00×/7.79× 是"在同一模型/同一度量下定向击败 SiliFuzz 风格无导向变异"，不是击败 Harpocrates。

### 0.3 现 paper2 的 4 处 best-paper 硬伤（重构必改）
1. **对标失衡**：几乎只对 SiliFuzz；Harpocrates 只在 Related Work 一笔带过。best-paper 须把 Harpocrates 作为头号相关工作，逐条差异化（§0.2 五轴），否则审稿人一眼看出"作者没读最近的同方法竞品"。
2. **"击败 SiliFuzz"的声称边界模糊**：现稿说 D13 碾压 SiliFuzz，但 SiliFuzz 本身自承"work-in-progress, 不声称 novelty"；击败一个自承不成熟的系统不足以撑 best-paper。须重构叙事：击败的是**"operand-undirected coverage-guided 代理模糊"这一方法类**（SiliFuzz 是其代表，Harpocrates 也属另一类），贡献是 **directed-on-random 这一新方法类**，并用 AVF 定理给根因。
3. **评估深度不足 vs Harpocrates**：Harpocrates 评 7 结构、50+ µarch SFI 目标、gate-level FU stuck-at。现 paper2 仅 2 注入器（bit-flip + byte_lane_skew）、单 µarch（V110）。须**诚实补全威胁到有效性**，并扩展现有数据里已有但未充分呈现的维度（per-register ACE 分布、多 bit vs 单 bit、19 模板的结构覆盖广度）——在已有数据范围内最大化，不编造新实验。
4. **故事线偏"我击败了随机"而非"我解决了什么开放问题"**：best-paper 的叙事是"问题→为什么之前没人解决→我的洞察→证据→边界"。现稿偏结果罗列。须把"为什么 directed 必须在 random 之上（AVF 定理）+ 为什么固定值字典被证伪（逻辑掩蔽）"这条**可证伪的洞察链**提到主线，13 版演进路径作为可复现性产物而非炫技。

---

## 1. 目标会场与论文类型判定

**目标会场（按匹配度排序）**：
1. **ASPLOS**（Architectural Support for Programming Languages/Operating Systems/Hardware）——最佳匹配：系统+体系结构交叉，SiliFuzz/Harpocrates 均在此体系发表相关后续，Hardware Sentinel (ASPLOS'25)、SEVI (ASPLOS'26)、Aging-SDC (ASPLOS'24) 均在此。best-paper 量级。

# Paper Configuration Record (Phase 0)

> 锁定字段。后续所有阶段不得偏离，除非用户显式变更。

## 1. 论文类型与会场

| 字段 | 值 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| Type | full research paper | 非 vision/performance/short；含原创方法 + 真实实验数据 + 真机部署 |
| Discipline | computer architecture / systems | 生成方法（µarch）+ 真机集群部署（系统）交叉 |
| **Venue (primary)** | **ASPLOS** | ACM 引用格式；系统+体系结构交叉 mandate 最贴本文"生成方法+真机部署"贡献；SiliFuzz/Harpocrates 后续 + Hardware Sentinel (ASPLOS'25)/SEVI (ASPLOS'26)/Aging-SDC (ASPLOS'24) 均在此体系 |
| Venue (backup) | ISCA | 若投稿时判断 µarch 理论深度更受重视；IEEE 格式需转 |
| ReviewTargetContext (#683) | ASPLOS full-paper 评审标准：novelty / technical depth / significance / reproducibility / presentation | 审稿人侧重：是否有方法类创新、技术深度是否够、影响是否显著、可复现、写作质量 |
| Citation format | **ACM-style**（带 DOI） | ASPLOS 是 ACM 主办；与 SiliFuzz/Harpocrates 的引用习惯一致 |

## 2. 语言与交付

| 字段 | 值 |
|---|---|
| Primary language | **English**（投稿用） |
| Parallel language | **中文译本**（团队阅读用，独立撰写非机翻） |
| 交付形态 | 英文 LaTeX (.tex + .bib, ACM ASPLOS 模板) + 英文 Markdown + 中文 Markdown |

| 新稿落点 | `docs/paper2/` |

## 3. 词数与结构

| 字段 | 值 |
|---|---|
| Word count target | **12000–14000 词**（ASPLOS full paper 典型 12–14 页正文） |
| 现稿基线 | 约 9000 词 → 需扩约 30%（主要在 Background/Harpocrates 对标/Threats/Related Work） |
| Abstract | 双语；EN 200–250 词；ZH 300–400 字 |
| 关键词 | 5–7/语言 |
| Mandatory inclusions | Data Availability / Ethics / CRediT / CoI / Funding / **AI-use disclosure（ASPLOS 政策）** / Limitations（§9） |

## 4. 既有材料（全部已核实存在）

- `docs/paper/paper2_en.md` + `paper2_zh.md`（现稿，数据真实但对标仅 SiliFuzz）
- `docs/kunpeng920_sdc_research_report.md`（研究报告，D1–D13 全演进 + 4 板 446 核 + gem5-CHAOS 真实数据）
- `docs/paper/ref/` 17 篇参考文献（已 pypdf 抽取至 `/tmp/reftext/`）
- 真实工件：`seeds/gem5/sdc_probe_workload_d{1..13}.c` + `_random.c`、`scripts/d{1..13}_sweep.py` + `gem5_sweep_*`、`tools/sdc_mutator/evolution_engine.py`、`scripts/distributed_scan.py` + `collect_results.py`、`output/distributed/results.json`、19 个 `seeds/*.S` 微架构压力模板
- 源码事实（subagent 逐行核实）：`fuzzer/program_mutation_ops.cc:187` TODO 证仅 bit-flip 一模式；`util/platform.cc:165-167` 证 Kunpeng `0x48`→N1 force-map；`runner/runner.h:32-43` 证 RunSnapOutcome 7 值；`proxies/arch_feature_generator.h:33-42` 证 per-bit toggle 信号存在

## 5. 诚实红线（贯穿全流程，不可违背）

1. **100% 真实数据**：每条数字可追溯到 on-disk 文件或命令输出；不编造新实验/数字/引文。
2. **3.00× 而非 3.07×**：B bit-flip = 41/500 = 8.2%（on-disk 重计），ratio 3.00×（z=7.00, p=2.5e-12）。`kunpeng920_sdc_research_report.md` §7.1 的 "3.07x" 是旧 8.0% 口径，正文不得沿用。§7.1 Footnote 1 保留差异说明。

- 双语 = 英文主稿 + 中文译本并行

# Literature & Positioning (Phase 1)

> 基于 17 篇参考文献深读（pypdf 抽取至 `/tmp/reftext/`）+ 两个 subagent 摘要整合。此文件是 Related Work 与 §2.3 对标 Harpocrates 的素材源。

---

## 1. Related Work 矩阵（按方法类聚类）

### 1.1 类 A：代理模糊 + 集群回放（operand-undirected）

| 论文 | 问题 | 方法 | ISA/µarch | 评估 | 头条数字 | 局限 | 与本文关系 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SiliFuzz** [VERIFY: Serebryany et al.] | 集群规模 SDC 扫描 | Unicorn 代理 + XED/ifuzz + Centipede coverage-guided；`FlipRandomBit` 对整条指令编码做随机位翻转（`program_mutation_ops.cc:187` TODO 证仅一模式）；snapshot → nolibc/seccomp runner → orchestrator 集群回放 | x86_64 | Google 生产集群部署 | ~500K snapshot；45% 发现独特； Unicorn/XED 占 40% 发现，ifuzz 20%，40% 共有 | 自承"work-in-progress, 不声称学术 novelty"；operand-undirected；无 µarch 反馈；无故障模型 | **基线 B 的来源**。本文复用其 toolchain（snapshot/snap/runner/orchestrator），替换其变异 |
| **Fleetscanner/Ripple** [VERIFY: Dixit et al. 2022, arXiv:2203.08989] | 集群 SDC 测试基础设施 | Fleetscanner（维护窗口 piggyback，分钟级）+ Ripple（生产并跑，毫秒级）；4 加速因素（数据随机/电气/环境/生命周期） | x86 (Meta) | Meta 集群，3+ 年 | Fleetscanner 93% 覆盖 / Ripple 77% / 合并 ~100%；Ripple ~12× 更快达等效覆盖 | 厂商特定测试知识；仅一缺陷族量化；无故障注入验证；无生成器 | 部署范式。本文 runner/orchestrator 是其开源类比；本文生成器填补其测试库缺口 |

### 1.2 类 B：µarch-aware 生成 + gem5 评估（最危险竞品）

| 论文 | 问题 | 方法 | ISA/µarch | 评估 | 头条数字 | 局限 | 与本文关系 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Harpocrates-HIL (ISCA'24)** [VERIFY: Karystinos et al., DOI 10.1109/ISCA59077.2024.00045] | 自动生成短功能测试程序最大化故障检测 | MuSeqGen（MicroProbe 之上，x86-64 生成器）+ 指令替换变异 + gem5 评估器 + ACE/IBR fitness + SFI 金标准；7 结构（IRF/L1D/LSQ/int add-mul/SSE FP add-mul）；>50 µarch SFI 目标 + gate-level FU stuck-at | x86-64 / AMD EPYC 7402 gem5 OoO | gem5 SFI；MiBench/SiliFuzz/OpenDCDiag 基线 | 30× SiliFuzz 生成率；99% int-adder 检测仅 50K cycles（vs MiBench 11M，220× faster）；99.5% vs SiliFuzz-best 86.6%（multiplier）；前缀切片（permanent FU 故障用前 10% 指令可检测） | **x86-64 only；gem5-only 无真机缺陷硅片；无真实缺陷类结构故障模型；静态操作数策略无 runtime directed-on-random；无集群噪声分类法** | **头号竞品**。本文差异化五轴（见 §2） |
| **Harpocrates++ (IEEE Micro Jan/Feb 2026)** [VERIFY: Karystinos et al., DOI 10.1109/MM.2025.3640385] | 同上，扩展 | 同 ISCA'24 + 随机种子方差实验 + 前缀切片实验 + Ripple/Fleetscanner framing | x86-64 / 同上 | 同上 | 随机种子方差 <1%（多数）至 ~17%（int mul）；前缀 0.1× 即可检 permanent FU 故障；0.01× 仅 SSE FP mul 跌至 0% | 同上 + "operand allocation via static policy, RL 是未来工作" | 同上。**显式自承 operand allocation 仍是静态策略 + "RL 是 add-on 未来工作"——本文 directed-on-random 正填此轴** |

### 1.3 类 C：集群 SDC 刻画（fleet characterization，x86）

| 论文 | 问题 | 方法 | ISA/µarch | 头条数字 | 局限 | 与本文关系 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SOSP'23 Understanding SDCs** [VERIFY: Wang et al., DOI 10.1145/3600006.3613149] | 首个大规模生产集群 SDC 定量研究 | >1M 处理器，32 月测试；633 厂商 testcase + 框架；27 故障处理器深研；Farron 缓解 | x86 (Alibaba) | 3.61‱ CPU 致 SDC；新片不更安全；温度线性相关（Pearson >0.75）；FP fraction 部分最脆弱 | 厂商工具链非公开；x86 only；无生成器；"560/633 testcase 检不出东西"+ "多线程未覆盖" | 互补。本文针对其 Observation 11（测试低效）缺口；ARM 服务器是其未覆盖 |
| **Veritas (HPCA'25)** [VERIFY: Chatzopoulos et al.] | 永久 gate-level FU 故障建模 + 集群 DPPM | ArithsGen 生成 gate-level FU 模型入 gem5 IEW；3000 注入/FU/µarch（1500 stuck-at-0+1）；5 µarch；Meta 6 年 DPPM | x86 / 5 OoO µarch | vector >> scalar 致 SDC；FP-heavy 最高；scalar int adder 最不易；CPU B 最高 1.59× CPU E | x86 only；permanent stuck-at only；相对率（绝对 DPPM 机密） | 方法论竞品。本文差异化：ARM + Unicorn 代理（非 gem5 self-grading）+ 真实缺陷硅片 |
| **PinDrop (HPCA'26)** [VERIFY: Mei et al.] | 持续测试刻画 SDC | IRMS + 1000+ 测试 9 族；110+ 特征；6 年 >500M 测试执行 | x86 (Meta, 8 arch A-H) | 0.035% 机器终生失败；0.0024%/季度稳态；>71% 持续 ≥2 年；vfm 最高失败率 | 根因未定（无 FA）；arch 匿名；无生成器 | 互补刻画。本文是其"所需生成侧"——PinDrop 缺的正是定向生成测试 |
| **SEVI (ASPLOS'26)** [VERIFY: Mei et al.] | 向量指令 SDC 分析 + ABFT 检测 | 2 阶段集群方法；246 testcase AVX2/FMA3/BMI；NumPy matmul；ABFT row/col checksum | x86 (Meta, 7 arch) | 28M SDC 事件；FMA 占 92%；98.5% 单 lane；FP SDC 翻 exponent（非仅 mantissa），相对误差达 10240；ABFT 88-100% 覆盖，1.35% 开销 | x86 AVX only；ABFT 仅 matmul；非向量 SDC 不检 | 向量 SDC 竞品。本文差异化：ARM SVE/NEON + 代理模糊语料 vs ABFT |
| **ITHICA** [VERIFY: arXiv:2605.15638] | 不一致错误（同指令同输入不同错果）检测 | 4 LLVM-IR 变换（Arith/Mem/MemDiv/Br）；>3000 隔离服务器；20-server DPool | x86 (>10 µarch, 2 vendor) | 检出比 SiliFuzz 多 69%；1.78× EDR；Arith 最有效；仅 1/14 单指令测试可复现 | x86 only；不检一致错误；排除 atomic/volatile | 直接竞品（指令复制 SDC 检测）。本文差异化：ARM + CHAOS 受控注入（含结构 byte-lane-skew）vs 依赖自然缺陷集群 |
| **Hardware Sentinel (ASPLOS'25)** [VERIFY] | 应用层症状 SDC 检测 | 内核/SEL 日志关联；30 天回溯；6 reboot/30d 阈值；FA 7/10 复现 | x86 (Meta, 7 gen) | +74% over Fleetscanner，+92% over Ripple，+41% over 合并；rare exception 过表征 | 离线分析；需丰富遥测；依赖应用崩溃（非崩溃 SDC 漏检） | 正交互补。本文覆盖其"非崩溃静默 SDC"盲点 |

### 1.4 类 D：在线检测（runtime，应用层）

| 论文 | 问题 | 方法 | ISA | 头条数字 | 局限 | 与本文关系 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Orthrus (SOSP'25)** [VERIFY] | 低开销在线 SDC 检测 | `#pragma user-data`/`closure` 注解 + LLVM 版本化内存 + 验证器进程异核重算 + 16-bit CRC 控制路径 + 采样调度 | x86 (Xeon Gold 6342) | ~4% 时间 / ~25% 内存开销；验证延迟 1.6 µs（Memcached）；97.2-98.9% 检测；1 核 87% / 2 核 91% / 4 核 96% | 不检 mercurial cores（离线测试的活）；不检 masked/control-branch/syscall 错误；需源码注解+重编译；x86 MIR 注入 | 不同层（runtime 应用级 vs 本文离线集群筛查）。Orthrus 自承"不检 mercurial cores"——留本文生态位 |
| **Vega/Aging-SDC (ASPLOS'24)** [VERIFY: Ma et al.] | 老化相关 SDC 自下而上检测 | BTI aging STA + Error Lifting（MUX 失败模型 + JasperGold 形式验证生成 cycle-accurate trace）+ LLVM pass 集成 | 32-bit in-order RISC-V (CV32E40P) | 100% ALU / 95.4-100% FPU 检测 vs random 35.3-97.2%；0.8% 运行时开销 | in-order 32-bit RISC-V only；ALU+FPU only；BTI aging only；门级网表非真老化硅片 | 互补。自下而上 vs 本文自上而下代理模糊；两者可互补 |
| **ITHICA**（见类 C） | — | — | — | — | — | — |

### 1.5 类 E：故障模型与传播（理论/刻画，非生成）

| 论文 | 问题 | 方法 | ISA/µarch | 头条数字 | 局限 | 与本文关系 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AVF theorem (MICRO'03)** [VERIFY: Mukherjee et al., DOI 10.1109/MICRO.2003.1253181] | 形式化 AVF = ACE-bits / total-bits | ACE lifetime 分析 | 通用 | 奠基性 | — | **本文根因框架**。AVF 定理预测：random 胜固定值字典（ACE 比例高），directed-on-random 更高 |

# Argument Blueprint (Phase 3)

> Claim→evidence 链 + 反论处理 + 可证伪性。这是 Phase 4 起草的论证骨架。

---

## 主 claim

**在 ARM 服务器 CPU（鲲鹏920/TaiShan V110）上，directed-on-random 变异生成 SDC 揭示工作负载，在 bit-flip 与真实缺陷类结构故障（`byte_lane_skew`）双度量下，极显著优于 operand-undirected（SiliFuzz 风格）变异。**

- **证据链**：
  1. D13 bit-flip 24.6% (123/500) vs B 8.2% (41/500)，3.00×，z=7.00, p=2.5e-12（极显著）→ Table III + Footnote 1（on-disk 重计诚实说明）。
  2. D13 structural 65.4% (327/500) vs B 8.4% (42/500)，7.79×，z=18.68, p≪1e-300（极显著）→ Table III。
  3. 同一模型（gem5 TaiShan V110 O3）、同一度量（500 单注入，ROI 20–80% 均匀随机周期）、同一注入器（CHAOSReg bit-flip / CHAOSLSQFwd byte_lane_skew）→ §2.4 + §5。

- **诚实边界（防过度声称）**：
  - 不声称击败 Harpocrates 的 99%——不同 ISA（x86 vs ARM）、不同故障模型（gate-level stuck-at vs byte_lane_skew）、不同结构（int adder/multiplier vs load-store-forwarding path）。
  - D13 vs B 是"同一模型同一度量下定向击败 operand-undirected 随机"，不是击败 Harpocrates 的 µarch-aware 生成。
  - 模型级 diverge 率（24.6%/65.4%）非硅片 SDC 率（gem5 O3 ≠ V110 RTL，§9）。

---

## 支撑 claim 1（为什么 directed 必须在 random 之上 — 根因）

**固定值操作数字典（all-0/all-1/alternating/boundary/subnormal/NaN，含 CSP 配对）被证伪，因逻辑掩蔽；AVF 定理预测 random 胜固定值，directed-on-random 胜二者。**

- **证据链**：
  1. Table I：A naive dict bit-flip 3.9% < B 8.0%（C/B=0.46×，p=0.0083）；structural 2.0% < 8.4%（0.33×，p=0.0001）。CSP-paired C 亦劣（bit 3.7%, struct 2.8%）。两度量统计显著劣 → `kunpeng920_sdc_research_report.md` §7.1。
  2. 根因机制（逻辑掩蔽）：结构化操作数产生确定性低熵结果；落在被结构化计算立即抵消的寄存器/位上的故障不可观测（如 `0xFFFFFFFF + 1 = 0` 丢弃高半）→ §4。
  3. AVF 定理预测：AVF = ACE-bits / total-bits；uniform 单注入下 diverge 率 = ACE 比例。random 把输出相关数据分散到更多寄存器/周期（高 ACE 比例），fixed-value 集中并抵消（低 ACE 比例）→ §3.1 + §7.2。
  4. **排除替代解释（PRNG 结构）**：LCG vs xorshift 每次调用熵统计相等（7.9817 vs 7.9782 bits/call）→ "random 胜因无数学结构"是民间说法；真因是 ACE 比例 → §7.2。
  5. ACE-fraction 扫描验证：B 7.6%（7 ACE 寄存器，PhysReg[4] 单 63% ACE）vs D5（字典超集）6.1%（10 ACE 寄存器，max 33%）。B 胜*尽管* ACE 寄存器更少，因其 ACE 寄存器各自承载远更多输出相关数据 → §7.2。

- **directed-on-random 的机制（为什么胜二者）**：`pick_high_toggle` runtime 生成两随机候选 A/B（同 B 覆盖广度），对 A 做定向变异（`A^mask; A+=1; rot; A^=~A`），评估 popcount carry-chain 代理（`popcount(A'^(A'+1))`），保留高代理者。= random 覆盖广度 + directed 高 ACE 偏向。不是魔术数字字典；运行时输出操作数看似随机高熵（反掩蔽）但偏向长进位链 → §4 + §5.2。

---

## 支撑 claim 2（可复现 — 13 版演进路径）

**13 版演进路径（D1–D13）每杠杆效应可见，含负杠杆，证明非 cherry-picking。**

- **证据链**：Table II 全 14 行（B + D1–D13），每行一杠杆：
  - D1 固定 toggle → 0.37× bit（劣）
  - D4 ACE-targeting backfire → 0.24× bit（**负杠杆**，证非 cherry-pick）
  - D7 去 volatile → 结构 0%（**杀结构**，证 volatile 是结构度量必需）
  - D8 混合 volatile → 结构 26.6%（3.17×，**首个统计显著超 B**）
  - D10 全 volatile + 16 操作数 → bit 8.0% = B 持平 + struct 17.0%（2.02×，**两度量都不低于 B**）
  - D12 跨循环 ACE → bit 12.4%（1.55×，**bit 首次显著超 B**）
  - D13 D12 + directed-on-random → bit 24.6% / struct 65.4%（**双极显著**）
  - 决定性转折 D12→D13：唯一新增杠杆是 `pick_high_toggle`，移 bit 12.4%→24.6% + struct 14.8%→65.4% → §7.3。

---

## 支撑 claim 3（部署 — 真机 0-SDC 是有意义测量）

**4 板 446 核真机部署，健康硅片 0 真 SDC；噪声分类法把 6016 runaway 噪声归零，证明"零"非检测缺失。**

- **证据链**：
  1. Table IV：0101(126核)/0102(192)/0103(128)/0201(96) 全板 outcome 2/3/4（真 SDC）= 0 → `output/distributed/results.json`。
  2. 与预期 10⁻⁸–10⁻¹⁰ per-execution 一致 → §7.4。
